steps.description: We start at the `public interface` every **synthetic Alchemix token** must implement. All bookkeeping and permission mechanisms we are interested in are defined here, extending the usual `ERC-20 API`.

`hasMinted(address)` is a read-only counter.  Whatever contract mints the token is expected to increase this number each time it creates new supply for `account`, allowing the system (and integrations) to track the lifetime total that address ever minted.

`lowerHasMinted(uint256)` lets an address *reduce* its own lifetime counter.  The comment says the call reverts unless the caller is on a whitelist – a safety valve for debt-reconciliation or migrations.

Administrators control two on-chain permission tables:
- `setCeiling(address,uint256)` – per-minter hard cap ("ceiling") on how many tokens that address may ever mint.
- `setWhitelist(address,bool)` – toggles whether an address may call privileged functions like `lowerHasMinted` or `mint`.

The core supply-changing hooks:
- `mint(recipient,amount)` – creates new synthetic tokens (and therefore new debt inside the Alchemist).
- `burn(amount)` – destroys caller’s tokens, removing debt.
Next we look at how the `Alchemist contract` (the lending engine) actually uses the `token interface`.

Inside the private `_mint` helper the Alchemist records debt on the NFT position (lines 714-721) and finally mints ERC-20 tokens to the user (line 724) via `TokenUtils.safeMint`, which in turn calls `IAlchemicToken.mint`.
Conversely, the public `burn` action removes debt and then destroys the caller’s tokens using `TokenUtils.safeBurnFrom` (line 472) – this calls `IAlchemicToken.burnFrom`/`burn` under the hood.
Tests show the typical admin flow: give the `Alchemist` unlimited minting head-room by whitelisting it and setting its ceiling to `type(uint256).max`.

Putting it all together:
- `hasMinted` & `ceiling` form a permanent ledger of how much any address has ever created.
- `lowerHasMinted` + `whitelist` let trusted actors correct that ledger when necessary.
- `AlchemistV3` is the primary minter/burner; it must be whitelisted and its ceiling configured at deployment.
These mechanisms provide transparent, on-chain constraints around synthetic supply while still keeping mint/burn logic inside the lending engine.
